newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain jails seven Shi'ites for arson attacks.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain jails seven Shi'ites for arson attacks.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court jailed seven Shi'ite Moslems for terms up to five and a half years on charges of arson attacks.
A court statement quoted by newspapers on Thursday said they had been found guilty of setting fire to 13 private vehicles, a commercial company, a garage and two cabins at private schools.

The court, whose judgment cannot be appealed, has jailed more than 220 Shi'ites since protests by members of the community broke out in December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Set up in March 1996 to speed up trials of government opponents, the court on Wednesday also adjourned a verdict against an eighth suspect because he had fled the country, the statement said.

On Saturday, a Bahraini court convicted six Shi'ites of possessing unlawful leaflets, but said the men should be set free because they had already spent 14 months in jail. They were also fined 200 dinars ($531) each.
More than 30 people have been killed in the unrest in Bahrain, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.
